## Highlights since 0.13.0

- **Chinese papers typeset and checked.** A new Chinese article template starts a ctex paper ready to compile, and when Chinese, Japanese or Korean text is missing from the PDF, the build says so and names the fix instead of leaving blank space. New templates also cover ACL/ARR, CVPR 2027, AAAI-27, ThuThesis and ustcthesis.
- **Rewrite a selection your own way.** Besides the built-in rewrites, you can now type any instruction for the selected text, such as "translate into academic English" or "shorten to about 100 words", and review the result before it replaces your text.
- **The agent uses your proxy.** The agent now starts with the proxy and model-provider settings from your login shell, so it works on networks that need a proxy without extra setup. When the system proxy changes, Lattice offers to restart the agent with the new one.
- **Grammar rules and errors in Chinese.** With the interface in Chinese, every grammar rule is named and explained in Chinese, and errors from the app itself are shown in Chinese too.

## Notable fixes

- Every way out of Lattice saves your work first, and an update never restarts the app on its own.
- Lattice's shortcuts work in the Agent panel and Git drawer, and ⌘W closes a tab.
- Pressing Enter or Escape to finish an input-method composition no longer submits, picks or cancels.
- Appearance, theme and build settings changed in one window apply to every open window right away.
- Each window is named for its project, and a large text file is called too large rather than binary.
- Double-clicking the title bar follows your macOS setting, and full screen keeps the window buttons in place.
- Updated the zip and KaTeX libraries past published security advisories.
